claims.text: Enhanced dynamic mechanical behavior in high-entropy alloys is primarily caused by a stress-induced in situ fcc-to-hcp transformation mediated by stacking-fault networks.
CrCoNi can have an initially single-phase fcc structure.
The proposed CrCoNi-based initial alloy has low stacking-fault energy.
Alloying or thermal treatment can raise stacking-fault energy and thereby suppress stacking-fault formation and the fcc-to-hcp transformation in the proposed alloy.
The controlled comparison should apply identical dynamic loading to a standard alloy and a variant designed to suppress stacking-fault formation.
Twinning and phase transformation become more active as temperature decreases from room temperature toward cryogenic levels.
Stacking-fault networks act as nucleation sites for an fcc-to-hcp transformation.
Fluctuations in local lattice friction promote the formation of stacking-fault networks.
Stacking faults nucleate localized hcp epsilon-martensite regions within an fcc matrix.
The newly formed hcp regions and their phase boundaries obstruct dislocation motion.
Continuous in situ transformation can provide the dominant contribution to strain hardening in a dual-phase Cantor-like HEA.
The fcc-to-hcp TRIP effect can enhance strain hardening to the benefit of strength and ductility.
Relative to a transformation-suppressed baseline, the transforming alloy will exhibit a higher strain-hardening rate.
Relative to the baseline, the transforming alloy will have greater ultimate tensile strength while maintaining or improving ductility.
The mechanism should apply broadly to multicomponent low-stacking-fault-energy fcc HEAs.
The mechanism should operate from room to cryogenic temperature at strain rates typical of mechanical testing.
Nanotwinning is a plausible competing deformation mechanism in CrCoNi-related fcc alloys.

A lack of significant differences in both phase evolution and mechanical properties between transforming and transformation-suppressed samples would falsify the proposed dominant-mechanism hypothesis.
